chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Shaybani (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i said, on the authority of his paternal uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, on the authority of Ali ibn Salim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Basir, on the authority of Abu Abd Allah Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High:
And they shall continue to differ, except those on whom your Lord has mercy; and for this did He create them.
He replied, “He created them to do what makes them deserve His Mercy so that He may have mercy on them.”
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah create humans with differences according to Surah Hud?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as) elucidates the verse from Surah Hud, interpreting human diversity not as chaos but as a deliberate divine design where differing natures allow individuals to earn mercy through their specific deeds. This explanation aligns with the Shia theological emphasis on 'al-hikmah' (divine wisdom), framing creation as a purposeful process of testing and rewarding rather than arbitrary variation. By highlighting that God created them 'for this,' the Imam underscores that the capacity for choice and subsequent merit is intrinsic to the human condition.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 10. that I asked Abu Abd Allah Ja`far al-Sadiq (as) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High:
